evidence: Workbook Quality Checks!C15 requires internally consistent synthetic seed data without orphan references or injection; Internal Quality Checks!E15:G15 says credentials inside the seed should be flagged. The only environment JSON/CSV/TSV file is task/environment/assets/seed_data.json. Its lines 2-3 contain an empty `snippets` array and a scope note: `No saved snippets are supplied in this seed. Build a JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history.` JSON parsing succeeded; zero records means there are no reference IDs or orphan rows. The sole free-text note contains no person, organization, contact detail, secret, role/tool override, or grading directive. This matches task/instruction.md:5, environment/instructions/integration.md:11, and tests/app_context.md:8, which explicitly allow no supplied snippets and an empty initial library. The frozen Dockerfile copies assets/ to /assets/, so this is the shipped seed. The read-only audit in per-row-review/evidence/14/seed_audit.json confirms the seed SHA256 30cf9958eca69569e0c78ca3ce4ec239c167dd41342baa361c10355b3d92e4b8 matches the manifest; the current raw index's 77 artifact hashes match. A broken app with no persistence would still pass this data-only row, so this verdict does not imply product quality. A conforming app that starts with an empty editor and library is explicitly allowed; no seeded identity is demanded by the judges. This was source/data inspection and a Python parse/hash audit, not a configured judge, Oracle, model, or portal run.
